trust_decision.summary: Whether an admin-configured integration URL may be dialed server-side when it resolves to a non-public address (or redirects there). At the pinned commit this is decided nowhere: Addon.fetchRetry passes the stored URL straight to ky, and create/update only check that required params exist. The fix decides it in validateUrl, called both at dispatch (fetchRetry, with DNS pinning and no redirect following) and at write time (AddonService.validateUrlParameter).

landing_point.why: The summary says the 'Addon webhook URL is dialed server-side', so a reader starts at the Webhook addon's fetchRetry(url, ...) call. It sends user-chosen customHeaders and authorization (webhook.ts:70-90), which is the header-exfiltration part of the summary.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Either way round: 'the runtime check in fetchRetry already blocks every dial, so save-time validation is only UX', or 'validating on create/update is enough, because stored configs were entered by an admin with CREATE_ADDON permission and are trusted'. The second leaves pre-existing rows and DNS rebinding or redirects open.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: 1) Updating an integration while the masked url '*****' is echoed back must keep working: the fix skips validation for MASKED_VALUE, and the existing value is merged back in. 2) Self-hosted deployments that point webhooks at internal hosts need an opt-out (allowPrivateUrlInIntegration) or a host allow-list. 3) Datadog with no url falls back to its public default URL. 4) A 30x response is returned as a status, not followed and not thrown. A fix that rejects every non-public address without an override, or that validates the masked placeholder, breaks these.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Slack App client built with a configurable slackApiUrl (for GovSlack or Enterprise Grid) taken from addon parameters, bypassing fetchRetry
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: WebClient accepts a slackApiUrl option, and region or alternative endpoints are a common feature request. A maintainer would wire it straight into new WebClient(...) rather than through Addon.fetchRetry.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a 'send test event' or 'test connection' admin route that dials parameters.url directly with ky before saving
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Integration UIs commonly add a test button. That route would naturally run before createAddon's validation and might call ky directly, the way the existing services do (src/lib/services/version-service.ts:1).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a new provider (e.g. a generic chat webhook) whose handleEvent calls ky/fetch itself instead of this.fetchRetry
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Each provider owns its own handleEvent, and nothing in the Addon base class forces use of fetchRetry.

Hidden-test design caveat: the published tests drive validation through an injected validateUrlOptions.lookup (fix.diff:490-492). A solver's API will differ, so behavioural tests should use literal IPs (127.0.0.1, ::ffff:127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254) and a local redirecting server. Also, defaultLookup returns a fake public IP under NODE_ENV=test (fix.diff:703-712), which belongs to the fix, not the pinned code.

The default-deny hurts fairness: the fix makes private URLs blocked by default and changes existing tests to opt in (fix.diff:1146, fix.diff:1158). The report must state the opt-out config names (allowPrivateUrlInIntegration / allowListIntegration), or hidden tests must not depend on them.
